sections.section_title: The Third Sign -- Seven Angels with Seven Last Plagues
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents the third heavenly sign -- seven angels carrying seven last plagues -- and declares that in them God's wrath is finished (etelesthē), identifying these plagues as a purposeful, finite act that brings God's judgment to its appointed conclusion within the Exodus pattern of covenantal plagues against the oppressor.

The neutral reading presents the conquerors standing on the sea of glass mixed with fire, having been victorious over the beast's threefold coercion (political worship, idolatrous image, economic mark), and singing a composite song of Moses and the Lamb that praises God's righteous character and envisions all nations voluntarily coming to worship.
sections.relevance: The conquerors' standing before God is presented as the direct outcome of genuine human choices under extreme duress. The neutral reading identifies their victory as fulfilling the promises made to 'the one who overcomes' in the seven letters -- promises with salvation-relevant outcomes including the tree of life (2:7), immunity from the second death (2:11), and a name in the book of life (3:5). The threefold specification of what they conquered -- ek tou thēriou, ek tēs eikonos autou, ek tou arithmou tou onomatos autou -- mirrors the threefold coercion of chapter 13, and the neutral reading states that 'each form of coercion was faced and overcome' and that 'those who stand on the sea of glass refused all three.' Their means of conquest, recalled from 12:11, include two genuinely human actions alongside divine provision: 'the word of their testimony' and their refusal to 'love their life even when faced with death.' The neutral reading also notes that the beast 'overcame' them physically (13:7), yet the same people are the true victors -- their victory was won through active resistance, not through irresistible divine action that bypassed their agency. The song's declaration that 'all the nations will come and worship before You' is interpreted in the neutral reading as suggesting 'voluntary movement,' with the parallel in Psalm 86:9 and Isaiah 2:2-3 describing nations who come freely.
key_phrases: those who were victorious over the beast and his image and the number of his name
they did not love their life even when faced with death
all the nations will come and worship before You
the faithful conquer by refusing to yield, even at the cost of their lives

sections.section_title: The Heavenly Temple Opens and the Angels Emerge
sections.summary: The neutral reading presents the opening of the heavenly temple of the tabernacle of testimony, the emergence of seven angels in priestly garments mirroring the risen Christ's attire, the delivery of golden bowls of wrath by a living creature from the innermost divine court, and the filling of the temple with smoke from God's glory and power so that no one can enter until the plagues are completed -- establishing that the coming judgments proceed from God's covenant presence, are executed by royal-priestly agents, and are irreversible once begun.
